question: A shop makes 30p on each £1 of sales. Cutting prices 10%, how many more sales keep its profit level?
answer: 50% more. After the cut, each old £1 of goods brings in 90p, of which 20p is profit instead of 30p, so the shop must sell 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 times as much. Discounts eat margins fast: a 20% cut would need three times the sales.
move: A discount comes straight out of the margin, so judge it against the margin.
ask: Which discount have I offered, or taken, without working out what it costs?

scene.readout: Extra sales needed to break even

notes.text: A 5% cut needs 20% more sales just to stand still.
10% off: half as many sales again, for the same profit.
25% off leaves 5p a pound of profit: six times the sales.

source: Nagle and Müller, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing, 2018
reference: Thomas T. Nagle and Georg Müller, The Strategy and Tactics of Pricing, sixth edition, Routledge, 2018
